plain: We could not follow it from year to year: in single WISE epochs it is too faint or sits on other stars, so its motion is not measured here. Stacking all WISE images along its catalog motion (0.34 arcseconds per year) does show it (signal-to-noise 45), so it is there, just too faint to follow year by year.
Its infrared colour W1-W2 = 0.71 mag is red, as for early-T and the reddest L brown dwarfs (dusty or very cool stars can look like this too).
Its brightness rises and falls regularly, every ~405 days (~126 or ~330 days fit the twice-yearly WISE visits equally well).
SPHEREx does not clearly detect it at 3.5-5 micrometres, so its spectrum cannot be typed.
